title: PRESIDENT OF INDIA HOSTS PRESIDENT OF THE SWISS CONFEDERATION
subtitle: CLOSE COOPERATION BETWEEN INDIA AND SWITZERLAND CAN BRING IMMENSE BENEFITS TO OUR PEOPLE: PRESIDENT DROUPADI MURMU
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                05 OCT 2026 10:40PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The President of India, Smt. Droupadi Murmu received H.E. Mr Guy Parmelin, President of the Swiss Confederation at Rashtrapati Bhavan today (October 5, 2026). She also hosted a banquet in his honour.
Welcoming President Parmelin to India, the President said that India and Switzerland enjoy warm and cordial relations based on the shared values of democracy and the rule of law. We have extensive cooperation across a wide range of areas, including trade and investment, science, technology and innovation, culture, and people-to-people contacts. Regular high-level exchanges between our two countries have continued to provide momentum to our bilateral relations.
The President said that Switzerland is an important trade and investment partner for India. She noted that following the implementation of the historic India-European Free Trade Association Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement, there are even greater opportunities for expanding bilateral trade and investment.
The President noted that Swiss companies have invested in India in important sectors and they have a notable presence in India’s infrastructure sector, particularly in the construction of roads, railway bridges and tunnels. She said that they can also explore opportunities in emerging areas such as clean and green technology and Artificial Intelligence.
The President was happy to note that important agreements have been signed during the visit to promote cooperation in migration and mobility, research, and technology transfer.
The two leaders agreed that close cooperation between India and Switzerland can bring immense benefits to the people of both countries. They expressed confidence that this visit will contribute to further strengthening relations between the two countries.

title: English Translation of Press statement by the Prime Minister during the Joint Press Statement with the President of Switzerland
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                05 OCT 2026 2:26PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Your Excellency, Mr. President,
Delegates from both countries,
Friends from media,
Namaskar!
I am very happy to warmly welcome the President of Switzerland to India.
First of all, I appreciate his commitment to India-Switzerland relations. In October last year, with his personal support, we implemented a historic Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement between India and the European Free Trade Association (EFTA) countries. This is India’s first FTA with any economic bloc in Europe.
It is also an ambitious blueprint for investment, innovation, jobs, and shared prosperity. Through this, we aim to achieve the targets of $100 billion in investment in India and 1 million direct jobs over the next 15 years.
Friends,
The friendship between India and Switzerland goes back centuries. In the 19th century, Swami Vivekananda saw a glimpse of the Himalayas in the Swiss Alps. Mahatma Gandhi also spent time in Switzerland and interacted with its people. The memories of these historic visits continue to resonate in our friendship even today.
Today, innovation, infrastructure, and advanced technology are strong pillars of our partnership. And through today’s summit, we are going to give our partnership a new momentum and take it to new heights.
Friends,
We have taken several important decisions to increase market access for Indian exports in Switzerland and further facilitate investment between the two countries.
This will help increase exports of Indian agricultural products, pharmaceuticals, textiles, and engineering goods to Switzerland. At the same time, we will attract new Swiss investments into key sectors in India, such as biotechnology, life sciences, banking, insurance, food processing, and sustainability. Through these initiatives, we will work together to develop trusted supply chains and reliable solutions for the world.
Friends,
Today, we identified new opportunities for cooperation in military exchanges and defence production. We also agreed to further deepen cooperation in nuclear energy.
The Varanasi ropeway, Jewar Airport in Noida, and railway and tunnelling projects in mountainous areas are shining examples of our infrastructure cooperation. To further strengthen this cooperation, today we signed an agreement on transport, mobility, and infrastructure.
We invite Swiss infrastructure companies to invest in India at a large scale and participate in capacity building, design, and manufacturing.
Friends,
Science and technology cooperation is also a strong pillar of our partnership. I am very pleased that we will soon launch new joint research projects in priority areas such as health, clean energy, and space. We also welcome the agreement with the University of Zurich to build the capacity of India’s science start-ups.
Given the growing popularity of Yoga and Ayurveda in Switzerland, we also had a meaningful discussion today on deepening cooperation in these areas.
Friends,
People-to-people ties are the greatest strength of our partnership. The Migration and Mobility Partnership Agreement and the Young Professionals Agreement signed today will open up many new opportunities in Switzerland for Indian students, researchers, professionals, and young people.
Friends,
Both India and Switzerland believe in democratic values, the rule of law, dialogue, and diplomacy. We will continue to work together for global peace and stability.
Whether it is Ukraine or West Asia, India has consistently supported every meaningful effort towards peace.
We also agree that reforms in global institutions are essential to address the growing global challenges.
Friends,
I am grateful to the President of Switzerland for visiting India with a large business delegation. On October 7, in his presence, we will host the “Prosperity Summit” with India-EFTA business leaders. This summit will serve as an important platform to turn the promise of our trade and investment partnership into concrete outcomes. I also extend my very best wishes to all the business leaders participating in this summit.
Your Excellency,
In February this year, India hosted the world’s largest AI Summit. Next year, Switzerland will take this journey forward through the “Geneva AI Summit.” I extend my best wishes to Switzerland for the success of the Geneva AI Summit. I am confident that together, we will continue to work towards making AI responsible, inclusive, and human-centric.
Once again, thank you very much for your visit to India and for being a strong supporter of India-Switzerland relations.

title: Integrated Ayurveda-Yoga Approach Shows Encouraging Results in Management of Bedwetting Among Children: ITRA Study
subtitle: Combination of Ayurvedic medicine and yoga asanas reported up to 70% improvement in nocturnal enuresis
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                05 OCT 2026 4:07PM by PIB Delhi
content:
A clinical study conducted at the Institute of Teaching and Research in Ayurveda (ITRA), Jamnagar, an Institution of National Importance under the Ministry of Ayush, Government of India, has reported encouraging results from an integrated approach combining Ayurvedic medicine with yoga asanas in the management of nocturnal enuresis, commonly known as bedwetting, among children.
The eight-week study involving approximately 38 children in the age group of 6–14 years found that children receiving Ayurvedic medicine along with regular practice of selected yoga asanas showed greater improvement compared to those receiving Ayurvedic medicine alone. The findings have been published in the internationally recognised AYU Journal.
Study Conducted in Two Groups
The study was conducted by the Department of Kaumarbhritya (Paediatrics), ITRA, Jamnagar. The participating children were divided into two groups.
Group 1 – Ayurvedic Medicine Alone:
Children received Medhya Rasayana Churna, a formulation comprising Brahmi, Shankhpushpi, Yashtimadhu (liquorice) and Guduchi, administered twice daily with milk.
Group 2 – Ayurvedic Medicine with Yoga:
Children received the same Ayurvedic formulation along with four yoga asanas — Utkatasana, Ardha-Shalabhasana, Bhujangasana and Shavasana — practised regularly in the morning and evening.
Significant Improvement Reported
The study reported encouraging outcomes across several parameters:
Reduction in bedwetting: Children receiving the Ayurvedic formulation alone showed approximately 38% improvement in the frequency of bedwetting, while those receiving the combined intervention of Ayurveda and yoga showed approximately 70% improvement.
Improvement in memory: An approximately 61% improvement in memory was reported among children receiving the combined intervention, compared to around 31% among those receiving the Ayurvedic medicine alone.
Reduction in irritability: Children in the combined intervention group showed approximately 66% reduction in irritability, along with improvements in behavioural parameters.
Reduction in hyperactivity: Regular yoga practice was associated with approximately 71% reduction in hyperactivity, with encouraging improvements also observed in concentration and morale.
The research paper was conducted and presented by Prof. Vaidya Virendra Kori, Vaidya Sagar Bhinde and Vaidya Amisha Bavarva. The researchers undertook a detailed analysis of the data generated during the study, following which the research paper was accepted for publication in the AYU Journal.
According to Prof. Dr. Tanuja Nesari, Director, ITRA, Jamnagar, nocturnal enuresis may, in some cases, be associated with difficulties in bladder control as well as psychological and behavioural factors.
The study indicates that selected yoga practices, including Utkatasana and Bhujangasana, may support strengthening of the pelvic region and better bladder control. Ayurvedic ingredients such as Brahmi and Shankhpushpi have traditionally been used for their calming properties and their role in supporting mental well-being.
The findings highlight the potential of an integrated approach combining Ayurveda and yoga in the management of nocturnal enuresis among children. The study also underlines the importance of integrating appropriate lifestyle practices with traditional systems of medicine for promoting overall health and well-being.
It may be noted that bedwetting is a common condition among children and should be addressed with sensitivity and appropriate medical guidance.

title: UCIL Celebrates Diamond Jubilee Year, Marks Six Decades of India’s Uranium Mining and Processing Capability
date:

content:
Uranium Corporation of India Limited, a PSU under the Department of Atomic Energy, celebrated its Diamond Jubilee Year, marking six decades since its incorporation on 4 October 1967 and its contribution to India’s nuclear power programme
Ms. Seema Jain, Member-Finance, Atomic Energy Commission, graced the celebrations at Jaduguda as the Chief Guest; she visited the Technology Demonstration Pilot Plant and the proposed new site of the Dark Matter Laboratory of the Saha Institute of Nuclear Physics, an aided institution of DAE
A first-of-its-kind Journalists’ Workshop provided the media delegates with an opportunity to gain first-hand experience of UCIL’s operations
A special DAE Technology Exhibition for the school students showcased the industrial and societal applications of nuclear energy
The celebrations showcased UCIL’s evolving capabilities in uranium mining and processing, while reflecting on its historical and continued contributions to India’s nuclear energy programme
The Uranium Corporation of India Limited (UCIL), a Public Sector Enterprise under the Department of Atomic Energy (DAE), celebrated its Diamond Jubilee Year on 4 October 2026, marking six decades of its journey in uranium mining and processing and its contribution at the forefront of India’s nuclear power programme.
The Diamond Jubilee Year celebrations at Jaduguda brought together senior officials, scientists, engineers, technical personnel, employees, media professionals and other stakeholders to commemorate an important milestone in UCIL’s institutional journey and to look ahead to the opportunities and shared responsibilities of the future.
The Diamond Jubilee Year celebrations were graced by Ms. Seema Jain, Member-Finance, Atomic Energy Commission, as the Chief Guest. During the programme, she also visited the Technology Demonstration Pilot Plant (TDPP) at C, R&D, Jaduguda, and the proposed new site of the Dark Matter Laboratory at the 815-metre level of the Jaduguda underground mine.
Speaking on the occasion, Ms. Seema Jain, Member-Finance, Atomic Energy Commission, said,
“The Diamond Jubilee Year of UCIL is a celebration of six decades of scientific capability, institutional experience and dedicated service to the nation. It is also an occasion to pay respectful homage to Dr Homi Jehangir Bhabha and the pioneers who laid the foundations of India’s uranium mining and processing capabilities. From the depths of the earth to the larger nuclear energy programme, UCIL has played an important and responsible role in building indigenous capability in uranium mining and processing. Over these six decades, generations of UCIL personnel have demonstrated remarkable dedication and grit, working in challenging conditions and environments to sustain this important national endeavour. As India looks towards an expanded role for nuclear energy, this milestone is also an opportunity to recognise the people, technologies and systems that have sustained this journey and to look ahead with confidence.”
Dr Ajit Kumar Mohanty, Secretary, Department of Atomic Energy and Chairman, Atomic Energy Commission, conveyed his greetings on the occasion and said,
“The Diamond Jubilee Year is an occasion to recognise the contributions of UCIL and to reaffirm the importance of continued innovation and capability building as India advances on the Nuclear Energy Mission.”
A significant feature of the Diamond Jubilee Year programme was the Journalists’ Workshop, organised at the Information Centre, Narwapahar, along with a DAE Technology Exhibition showcasing technologies and applications emerging from the DAE’s Units and Institutions.
The workshop brought participating media delegates closer to the science, technology and people behind India’s nuclear power programme. It provided the media delegates with an opportunity to interact with scientists, engineers and technical experts and gain a deeper understanding of the technologies, systems and applications that constitute the wider nuclear and radiation technology ecosystem.
The media delegates visited UCIL’s uranium mining and milling facilities, gaining first-hand exposure to mining operations, ore handling and processing systems, as well as the technologies and practices adopted at the operational sites.
Dr. Kacham Anand Rao, Chairman & Managing Director, UCIL, said:
“The Diamond Jubilee Year is a proud milestone for every member of the UCIL family. Over six decades, UCIL has steadily built expertise and infrastructure in uranium mining and processing, while strengthening its capabilities in technology, safety and environmental management. We were particularly pleased to open our operations and facilities to the media on this occasion. The Journalists’ Workshop and DAE Technology Expo provided an opportunity for first-hand engagement with the science, technology and people behind our operations and with the wider contributions of DAE.”
Established in 1967, UCIL has been an integral part of the development of India’s indigenous uranium mining and processing capabilities, providing the essential resource base for India’s nuclear power programme. The Diamond Jubilee Year celebrations marked the evolution of a specialised national capability, from underground and opencast mining to ore processing, technology development, occupational safety, radiation protection and environmental management.
Six decades of experience. A continuing commitment to capability. And a renewed journey towards the future of India’s nuclear energy programme. Uranium Leads the Way.

title: From Coal Availability to Energy Security: CIL Strengthens Coal Supply and Distribution to Power Sector
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                05 OCT 2026 2:15PM by PIB Delhi
content:
For India's power sector, Coal is an essential component of the country's energy-security chain—linking mining, evacuation, power generation and electricity availability. In this chain, Coal India Limited (CIL), which supplies nearly four-fifths of its coal to the Power Sector, occupies a pivotal position.
The recent performance of CIL demonstrates a clear strengthening of this supply chain. FY 2026-27 has witnessed a marked improvement in coal offtake and power-sector supplies over the corresponding period of the previous year, supported by enhanced evacuation, better synchronisation of production and despatch, and utilisation of accumulated pithead stocks.
The numbers tell the story.
Supply momentum gains strength
During the first six months of FY 2026-27, CIL's total coal offtake reached 384.2 Million Tonne (MT), compared with 357.0 MT during the corresponding period of FY 2025-26—an increase of 27.2 MT or 7.6%.
The momentum strengthened considerably in the second quarter. CIL's Q2 offtake rose to 186.04 MT, compared with 166.04 MT in Q2 of FY 2025-26, representing a growth of 12.05%. Thus, the improvement was not confined to a single month but became progressively more pronounced during the quarter.
September provided a stronger signal. CIL's total coal supplies during the month rose to 61.20 MT, against 54.40 MT in September 2025, registering a growth of 12.5%.
Indeed, CIL liquidated 63 MT of pithead coal stocks during the first half of FY 2026-27, demonstrating that increased supply was supported not only by current production but also by better inventory utilisation.
Power Sector remains at the centre of the supply strategy
The significance of these numbers becomes clearer when viewed through the lens of the Power Sector.
During H1 FY 2026-27, CIL's power-sector coal despatch stood at 302.8 MT, compared with 285.4 MT during H1 FY 2025-26. This represents an increase of 17.4 MT or 6.1%.
In other words, nearly 79% of CIL's total H1 offtake was directed towards the Power Sector, reaffirming the primacy of power generation in CIL's distribution strategy.
The Q2 performance is especially significant. CIL supplied 148.20 MT to the Power Sector in Q2 FY 2026-27, against 133.50 MT in Q2 of the previous year—a growth of 11%.
Thus, the improvement is increasingly becoming broad-based: higher total offtake is translating into higher supplies to power plants.
September: a strong supply response to rising power demand
September 2026 stands out as a particularly strong month for CIL.
Power-sector supplies increased from 44.20 MT in September 2025 to 48.90 MT in September 2026, an increase of 4.70 MT or 10.63%. At the same time, overall CIL coal supplies increased by 6.80 MT or 12.5%.
The distribution data also shows the intensity of the daily supply effort. During September 2026, CIL's power-sector despatch aggregated approximately 48.99 MT, equivalent to an average of around 1.63 MT per day. The first seven days averaged about 1.51 MT/day, while the last seven days averaged about 1.59 MT/day—an improvement of roughly 5% in daily throughput towards the end of the month.
Looking at the data since 28th September, the intensity of the daily supply effort is visible where the daily power-sector despatch remained robust, reaching 1.74 MT, 1.79 MT and 1.71 MT on 28–30 September, and sustaining the momentum in October at 1.75 MT, 1.87 MT and 1.81 MT on 1–3 October, respectively.
Thus, CIL has been able to sustain high-volume daily supplies during the closing phase of the monsoon period and into the post-monsoon operating window.
Supply improvement is reflected in power generation
The most important test of a coal-supply system is ultimately its ability to support electricity generation.
The available generation data shows a clear improvement in domestic coal-based generation during the first half of FY 2026-27.
Domestic coal-based generation increased to 640.05 BU in H1 FY 2026-27, compared with 582.5 BU during the corresponding period of FY 2025-26—an increase of about 57.5 BU or 9.9%.
From mine to power plant: distribution is becoming increasingly responsive
CIL's distribution architecture has progressively evolved from a predominantly linkage-based framework into a more diversified and responsive system.
Power-sector requirements continue to be served principally through Fuel Supply Agreements and linkage mechanisms, while short-term requirements can be supported through other market-based channels. At the same time, linkage rationalisation, digital systems, consumer-facing portals and improved logistics have contributed to greater supply flexibility and efficiency.
The result is an increasingly integrated supply chain in which production, stock, evacuation and consumer demand are managed as interconnected elements rather than as isolated activities.
The current performance also demonstrates the value of maintaining adequate pithead inventory. The availability of coal stocks at the beginning of the financial year provided CIL with the ability to sustain consumer supplies even while production was being progressively ramped up following the monsoon period.
The road ahead: from higher supply to assured supply
The improvement achieved during FY 2026-27 is encouraging, but the objective is larger than simply achieving a higher offtake number.
The ultimate goal is assured, predictable and quality-conscious coal supply.
CIL's ongoing investments in First Mile Connectivity, rapid loading systems, and digital monitoring are aimed precisely at achieving this transition. 46 CHP-silos provide 432 MT of mechanised close-loop evacuation capacity. CIL is contemplating more CHP-Silos in its greenfield mines that are about to come.
Coal supply as an instrument of energy security
The measure of success for CIL is increasingly not only how much coal is produced, but how reliably it reaches the consumer, how effectively it supports power generation, and how efficiently the entire coal supply chain responds to the country's energy requirements.
With the post-monsoon production build-up, expanding evacuation infrastructure, and continued focus on Power Sector requirements, the objective now is clear: a resilient energy supply for the nation.

title: Sanchar Saathi portal crosses 30 crore visits as citizens turn Cyber Warriors against telecom fraud
subtitle:
Over 14 lakh lost and stolen handsets recovered

More than 4 crore citizen requests on knowing mobile connections in their name resolved

Citizen reports on Sanchar Saathi portal also feed the Financial Fraud Risk Indicator, helping prevent suspected cyber-fraud losses of over ₹5,000 crore
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                05 OCT 2026 2:27PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Citizens across the country have visited the Sanchar Saathi portal (www.sancharsaathi.gov.in) more than 30 crore times since its launch in May 2023, reflecting the trust they place in it to protect themselves from telecom-related frauds. Developed by the Department of Telecommunications (DoT), the portal places simple and easy-to-use tools in the hands of every mobile user – to report a suspicious call or message, to know how many mobile connections are running in their name, to block a lost or stolen handset, and to check whether a handset is genuine before buying it.
Every visit to the portal protects the citizen, and every suspect communication that they report, protects many others. The information shared by citizens on Sanchar Saathi is converted into actionable intelligence that helps DoT, banks and law enforcement agencies to stop fraudsters before they reach their next target. Each citizen who uses Sanchar Saathi thus acts as a Cyber Warrior and as a shield against cyber frauds.
Services at the fingertips of every citizen
Sanchar Saathi brings the following citizen-centric services on a single platform:
Chakshu – Report suspected fraud communication and spam:
Report suspicious calls, SMS or WhatsApp messages – such as fake KYC or bill-payment alerts, impersonation of Government, police or bank officials, and fraudulent investment, job or loan offers – in a few simple steps.
Know mobile connections in your name:
Check all mobile connections issued on your identity and report those which you have not taken or no longer require, so that they cannot be misused.
Block your lost or stolen mobile handset:
Block the handset across the networks of all telecom operators so that it cannot be used anywhere in India, enable its tracing, and unblock it once it is found.
Know the genuineness of your mobile handset:
Verify a handset through its IMEI number before buying a new or second-hand phone.
Report incoming international calls with Indian numbers:
Report calls from abroad that are disguised as domestic (+91) numbers, helping the Government act against illegal telecom set-ups.
Trusted Contact Details:
Verify the genuine customer care numbers, email IDs and website links of banks and financial institutions before sharing any information.
Keep Yourself Aware:
Access awareness material on prevailing fraud trends such as fake loan apps, investment scams, fake job calls and fake traffic challans.
What citizens have achieved through Sanchar Saathi
The Sanchar Saathi dashboard reflects the scale of what citizens and DoT have achieved together:
More than 30 crore
visits to the Sanchar Saathi portal;
60.96 lakh
lost or stolen mobile handsets blocked,
37.85 lakh
traced and
over 14 lakh
recovered;
Over 4 crore
requests received from citizens to check and report mobile connections in their name have been resolved;
12.80 lakh
inputs on suspected fraud communications received through Chakshu, leading to action in
59.82 lakh
cases, including disconnection of
more than 50 lakh
mobile connections;
Suspected cyber-fraud losses of
more than ₹5,000 crore
prevented through the Financial Fraud Risk Indicator (FRI);
Jan Bhagidari: every citizen a Cyber Warrior
When a citizen reports a suspicious call or message on Chakshu, or flags a mobile connection that was never taken in his or her name, the benefit goes far beyond that one individual. Each such report alerts DoT to a mobile number, a device or a pattern being misused to defraud people, and enables timely action, including re-verification and disconnection, before more citizens are targeted. More than 50 lakh mobile connections have been disconnected on the basis of such citizen inputs. Citizens using Sanchar Saathi are therefore not merely beneficiaries of the platform; they are Cyber Warriors who protect their families, their communities and the nation.
Citizen reports power the Financial Fraud Risk Indicator and the Digital Intelligence Platform
The information contributed by citizens is one of the feeds for DoT’s wider fraud-prevention framework. It is a key input for the Financial Fraud Risk Indicator (FRI), which provides risk-based intelligence on mobile numbers potentially linked to financial fraud. This intelligence is shared securely through the Digital Intelligence Platform (DIP) with banks, payment service providers, telecom service providers and law enforcement agencies, enabling them to build telecom risk signals into their fraud detection and transaction monitoring systems and to alert or stop a suspicious transaction before the money leaves a citizen’s account. FRI has helped prevent suspected cyber-fraud losses of more than ₹5,000 crore. The Sanchar Saathi ecosystem feeds intelligence to over 1,600 stakeholders who are connected to the Digital Intelligence Platform enabling a
‘whole of government approach’
for coordinated action. A single report by a vigilant citizen thus travels across the telecom, financial and law-enforcement systems to protect many others.
More than 14 lakh lost and stolen handsets recovered
A citizen who loses a mobile handset can report it on Sanchar Saathi and have it blocked across all telecom networks in the country. If anyone attempts to use the blocked handset, its traceability is generated and shared with the police. Through continuous technical enhancements, automated workflows and close coordination among DoT, Telecom Service Providers and State/UT Police authorities, 60.96 lakh handsets have been blocked, 37.85 lakh traced and more than 14 lakh recovered so far.
Simple, multilingual and accessible
The Sanchar Saathi portal has been designed with simple and user-friendly service flows, supported by public dashboards and extensive awareness content on telecom safety, fraud prevention and responsible digital practices. The Sanchar Saathi mobile app, available in English, Hindi and 21 regional languages, brings the same services to citizens in their own language with the convenience of using it over their mobile.
DoT’s appeal to citizens
DoT urges every mobile user to visit Sanchar Saathi (
www.sancharsaathi.gov.in
) or use the Sanchar Saathi app, to check the mobile connections issued in their name, and to report every suspicious call, SMS or WhatsApp message. A few moments spent on the portal or while using the Sanchar Saathi app can protect a citizen, and many others, from fraud. Citizens who have already lost money or have become victims of cyber-crime should immediately report the matter on the cyber-crime helpline 1930 or at
https://www.cybercrime.gov.in

subtitle:
NCCSR 2026, on 6th–7th October in New Delhi, to provide a national platform for dialogue, collaboration and knowledge-sharing on CSR

CSR in India has its foundation in Indian tradition and in the concept of trusteeship, and did not emerge only from the Companies Act: Gyaneshwar Kumar Singh, DG  & CEO, IICA
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                05 OCT 2026 7:28PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Indian Institute of Corporate Affairs (IICA), under the aegis of the Ministry of Corporate Affairs, Government of India, observed CSR Day recently on the birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi. Shri Gyaneshwar Kumar Singh, Director General & CEO, IICA, delivered a Special Address to the Participants of Batch 11 of the IICA Certified CSR Professional Programme. The session, organised virtually by the School of Business Environment, IICA, also served as the curtain-raiser to the 3rd National Conference and Exhibition on Corporate Social Responsibility (NCCSR 2026).
The observance draws on a suggestion made by the then Hon'ble President of India, Shri Ram Nath Kovind, at the National CSR Awards in 2019, that 2nd October be dedicated to Corporate Social Responsibility. Rooted in Mahatma Gandhi's philosophy of trusteeship, IICA CSR Day provides a platform for dialogue, recognition, collaboration and knowledge-sharing on India's evolving CSR ecosystem.
Welcoming the DG & CEO, Dr. Garima Dadhich, Head, School of Business Environment and Course Director, said that what the CSR ecosystem needs in greater numbers is trained professionals with the capacity to turn an obligation into an outcome. She emphasised that the programme has been linked with the National Conference as part of its curriculum for this purpose, and
informed that NCCSR 2026 has drawn over 550 delegates from across India.
In his address, Shri Gyaneshwar Kumar Singh said that 2nd October and CSR are philosophically connected,
as CSR in India has its foundation in Indian tradition and in the concept of trusteeship, and did not emerge only from the Companies Act.
Referring to Section 166(2) of the Companies Act, 2013, he said the law itself recognises that a company operates within society and owes responsibility to its employees, the community and the environment, and not to shareholders alone.
Tracing the evolution of the framework, he said that CSR expenditure has grown from about ₹10,000 crore in the first year of the mandate to nearly ₹35,000 crore in FY 2023–24. He described the journey from the early "comply or explain" phase to the 2019 amendments and the 2021 Rules, which introduced the Unspent CSR Account, multi-year projects, certification of fund utilisation and impact assessment. He said that CSR should not be seen as deficit financing that merely supplements government spending. Its purpose is to leverage corporate resources, technology and expertise to create a multiplier effect and to test innovative approaches in the social sector.
He observed that a significant part of CSR remains supply-driven, with projects chosen on the basis of familiar areas, geographies and agencies, and called for needs-based CSR with community participation, a standard operating procedure for need assessment and social impact assessment, and stronger capacity among implementing agencies. He highlighted the CSR Exchange Portal of the Ministry as a platform on which district administrations, organisations and communities can place documented needs before companies, and also encouraged companies in the same sector to pool resources for high-impact national projects.
On Viksit Bharat, he said the goal should not be seen only in terms of the size of the economy and that "Viksit Bharat also requires developed thinking and a developed social consciousness," he said. He further concluded by calling for a shift from spending to transforming, from compliance to commitment, from reporting to evidence, and from isolated initiatives to collaboration, supported by technology-enabled monitoring, and urged the Participants to become ambassadors of this CSR philosophy.
NCCSR 2026 will be held on 6th–7th October 2026 at The Ashok, New Delhi, on the theme ‘
Re-envisioning the Spirit of CSR for Viksit Bharat: From Compliance to Commitment’
. It is being organised by the School of Business Environment, IICA, and will bring together senior representatives of Government, the corporate sector, Central Public Sector Enterprises, corporate foundations, implementing agencies, United Nations agencies, academic institutions and State Governments.
Along with five High Level Panels and a Fireside Chat spread across 2 days, the National Exhibition on CSR 2026 will also be held alongside the Conference, featuring 30–40 stalls organised around four thematic zones aligned with the Viksit Bharat @ 2047 vision: Yuva (education, skilling and employability), Garib (aspirational districts, tribal and marginalised communities), Annadata (agriculture and rural livelihoods) and Nari Shakti.

title: Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh Underscores India’s Rising Maritime Power, Indigenous Naval Capability and Strategic Strength at Barakhana in Visakhapatnam
subtitle:
Highlights Indian Navy’s growing combat prowess and its pivotal role in safeguarding India’s maritime interests

Calls for harnessing India’s vast maritime potential to drive national prosperity, economic growth and strategic power

Pays tribute to Naval Personnel and families for their courage, dedication and contribution to national security
date:

                05 OCT 2026 10:49PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh attended a Barakhana organised by the Eastern Naval Command in Visakhapatnam on October 05, 2026 and interacted with Indian Navy personnel and their families. He commended the naval personnel for their unwavering commitment to safeguarding the nation’s maritime interests and acknowledged the contribution and sacrifices of their families, whose support enables them to discharge their duties with dedication and commitment.
Addressing the gathering, Shri Rajnath Singh said the Barakhana provided an opportunity to interact with the naval fraternity and reaffirmed the Government’s appreciation of the dedicated service rendered by the personnel. He conveyed his continued support to the personnel and their families and recognised their commitment and contribution towards national security.
The Raksha Mantri highlighted the Indian Navy’s emergence as a powerful maritime force and its proven ability to respond decisively to challenges confronting the nation. He said the Navy’s capabilities are recognised across the Indo-Pacific and commended its personnel for remaining steadfast in all weather and operational conditions while ensuring the security of India’s maritime boundaries and keeping the Tricolour flying high. Recalling the Navy’s glorious record of valour, he referred to its decisive role during the 1971 War, particularly
Operation Trident
, when Indian naval forces struck Karachi harbour. He said the operation demonstrated the Navy’s capability not only to safeguard India’s maritime frontiers but also to project power and undertake offensive operations against the adversary when required. He paid tribute to the personnel whose courage and sacrifice continue to inspire generations.
Emphasising India’s transformation as a maritime power, Shri Rajnath Singh said the Indian Navy has kept pace with the changing security environment of the 21st century, with the country developing and inducting advanced and indigenous platforms, including indigenous aircraft carriers, nuclear submarines, stealth frigates and Scorpène-class submarines. He stressed that the strength of the Navy extends beyond ships, submarines and advanced technology and rests fundamentally on the professionalism, patriotism, courage and commitment of its personnel. He said India’s endeavour is to ensure that its waters reflect the nation’s maritime might, its warships embody Indian technology and the Navy’s operations reflect the country’s growing confidence and self-reliance.
Calling for a broader maritime vision, the Raksha Mantri said India must move forward with the philosophy of ‘advancing from the seas towards prosperity and power’, with the oceans viewed not merely as maritime boundaries requiring protection but also as an avenue for economic development, strategic influence and national prosperity.
Describing naval personnel as heroes and an inspiration to the youth, Shri Rajnath Singh said that they represent India’s future, India’s strength and India’s pride. He expressed confidence that their continued dedication and commitment would contribute significantly to India’s emergence as a stronger, more prosperous and self-reliant nation. He also underlined the important role played by the families of Defence Forces personnel, noting that while naval personnel remain deployed at sea in the service of the nation, their families shoulder responsibilities at home and provide the support and strength required for them to discharge their duties effectively. He described the service of the personnel and the sacrifices of their families as a valuable national asset.
Highlighting the informal and familial spirit of the Barakhana, Shri Rajnath Singh said that such occasions provide an opportunity to strengthen the bond between Defence Forces personnel, their families and the leadership. He observed that food is not merely a means of satisfying hunger but also a simple and profound expression of affection and togetherness, as people traditionally invite those with whom they share a special bond to their homes for a meal. He said the Barakhana similarly symbolised the deep relationship between the Defence Forces and the nation, with everyone coming together as part of one larger defence family.
The Raksha Mantri emphasised that the occasion was a reflection of the fraternity, camaraderie and sense of belonging that binds Defence Forces personnel, their families and the leadership. He highlighted the important role of families, noting that while naval personnel remain deployed at sea in the service of the nation, their families shoulder responsibilities at home and provide the strength and support that enable them to discharge their duties effectively. He said that the service of the personnel and the sacrifices of their families together constitute a valuable national asset.

content:
In a significant demonstration of India’s indigenous shipbuilding capabilities, Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh will launch Fleet Support Ship-1 (FSS-1), lay the keel of Fleet Support Ship-5 (FSS-5) and also inaugurate the upgraded Slipway-4 and 300-tonne Goliath Crane at Hindustan Shipyard Limited, Vishakapatanam, on October 06, 2026.

Three different technical sessions, focussing on rental housing, regulatory frameworks and affordable housing technologies and financing, brought together stakeholders to discuss approaches for expanding access to adequate and affordable housing.
Technical Sessions to Deliberate on Emerging Urban Housing Challenges
It featured thematic technical sessions on topics such as rental housing, bridging the Demand–Supply Gap in housing and role of innovative construction technologies in affordable housing sector, bringing together policymakers, experts, financial institutions, industry stakeholders and other partners to deliberate on key challenges and opportunities for building a stronger and more sustainable housing ecosystem.
The technical deliberations focused on three areas:
1. Structural Challenges and Enabling Measures for Unlocking the Potential of Rental Housing: The session examined the structural and institutional challenges affecting the availability and scalability of rental housing in urban areas. Discussions focused on creating an enabling ecosystem for Affordable Rental Housing, including suitable regulatory frameworks, land and infrastructure availability, investment mechanisms, effective property management and greater participation of public and private sector stakeholders.
The deliberations also explored measures to strengthen rental housing as a viable and dignified housing option for urban migrants, workers, students, working women and other mobile and vulnerable sections of the urban population.
2. Regulatory Measures to Bridge the Demand–Supply Gap in Housing: The second session focused on regulatory and policy measures required to address the persistent mismatch between demand and supply of affordable housing in urban areas. Deliberations covered the need for streamlined approvals, efficient land-use planning, enabling development regulations, improved coordination among stakeholders and measures to facilitate faster delivery of affordable housing.
3. Low-Cost Indigenous Technologies and Financing Instruments for Scaling Resilient and Affordable Housing: The third session focused on the role of innovative, low-cost and indigenous construction technologies in accelerating housing delivery while improving quality, resilience, resource efficiency and affordability.
The discussions emphasised the need to combine technological innovation with appropriate financing solutions to enable large-scale delivery of safe, climate-resilient and affordable homes.
The technical sessions underscored the need for a coordinated approach involving Government, States and UTs, Urban Local Bodies, financial institutions, private sector, technology providers, academia and other stakeholders to address the evolving housing needs of India’s rapidly urbanising population.
The World Habitat Day 2026 celebrations reaffirmed India’s commitment to ensuring that every urban household has access to safe, affordable and dignified housing, contributing to the broader vision of an inclusive and Viksit Bharat.

Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology and Earth Sciences and Minister of State for PMO, Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh today reiterated the Government’s commitment to ensuring Ease of Life and Pensioners’ Welfare, stressing that technology and digital interventions must ultimately translate into simpler and more accessible services for pensioners and their families.
Addressing the 17th Pension Adalat organised by the Department of Pension & Pensioners’ Welfare (DoPPW) at T. N. Chaturvedi Memorial Hall, IIPA, New Delhi, Dr. Jitendra Singh said that pension administration must continuously learn from the experiences and difficulties faced by pensioners and work towards removing shortcomings in the existing system. At today's Adalat 756 of 897 grievances were redressed, thus achieving 84.2% redressal rate.
he Minister lauded PM Sh Narendra Modi for introducing the concept of Pension Adalat in 2017.
The Minister emphasised the importance of identifying gaps in pension delivery and addressing them through continuous improvement. He said that the objective of pension reforms is not merely technological advancement but ensuring that the benefits of reforms reach the last mile and make a tangible difference to pensioners.
The 17th Pension Adalat took up 897 grievances relating to family pensioners and super-senior pensioners for expeditious redressal. As on October 5, 2026, 756 cases have been redressed, registering a redressal rate of 84.2 per cent. The remaining cases are being pursued for redressal in the coming days, reflecting the Government’s continued focus on timely grievance resolution and Pensioners’ Welfare.
Dr. Jitendra Singh highlighted the growing use of digital technology in pension-related services and said that efforts are being made to make processes simpler through digital identity and face-recognition based mechanisms. He stressed the need to continuously inform pensioners about such facilities so that they can make full use of the available digital services.
Referring to the Digital Life Certificate initiative, the Minister underlined the importance of campaigns and awareness programmes to ensure that pensioners are able to obtain digital certificates conveniently. He noted the significant scale achieved through such initiatives and stressed that greater awareness and outreach would further strengthen their impact.
Dr. Jitendra Singh also highlighted the role of media and public communication in taking pension reforms to pensioners across the country. Referring to the positive results achieved through earlier awareness campaigns, he called for continued efforts to use modern communication tools to ensure that pensioners and their families remain informed about available services and reforms.
The Minister further said that technology should be used not only for routine service delivery but also for identifying issues and improving the overall pension administration system. He said that wherever gaps or avoidable difficulties are noticed, they should be reported and addressed so that the system can continuously improve.
Dr. Jitendra Singh stressed that Pensioners’ Welfare remains central to the Government’s approach and that technological interventions should be accompanied by sensitivity towards the needs of pensioners and family pensioners.
The Minister also referred to the continuing efforts to simplify pension-related procedures and improve support for families of pensioners. He emphasised that reforms must remain focused on practical difficulties faced by beneficiaries and should contribute to greater Ease of Life.
The 17th Pension Adalat brought pensioners and concerned Ministries and Departments together for the presentation and consideration of pension grievances. The programme included the presentation of cases before Dr. Jitendra Singh by the Joint Secretary (Pension). The proceedings enabled grievances to be examined directly and facilitated coordinated efforts towards their expeditious redressal.
During the adalat, Flyers on Success Stories of the 16th Pension Adalat and the e-booklet “Bringing Ease in the Life of Family Pensioners” were released. The publications highlight the Government’s continuing efforts towards effective grievance redressal and improving the experience of pensioners and family pensioners.
The 17th Pension Adalat is part of the institutional mechanism developed by the Department of Pension & Pensioners’ Welfare for the meaningful, accessible and expeditious redressal of pensioners’ grievances.
An exemplary case of Ms. Chander Kanta Jally, whose husband made the supreme sacrifice in 1973. She was sanctioned Liberalised Family Pension. However, due to certain reasons, the family pension paid to her was lower than the amount to which she was entitled. She became aware of this and approached various forums. During the Pension Adalat, Sh. Jaswinder Jally, her son, attended through video conferencing from Chandigarh and presented the grievance on behalf of his mother before the Hon’ble MoS (PP). The case was discussed at length. Subsequently, family pension arrears amounting to Rs. 2.02 crore were released.
Another case involving Ms. Damyanti Sinha, with the help of the Pension Adalat, pensionary benefits of more than Rs. 72 lakh were released.
Both these cases involved super-senior family pensioners.

The Chintan Shivir, being held under the motto “Gatishakti se Pragati”, brings together Transport and PWD Ministers from States, senior officials of State PWDs, implementing agencies and other stakeholders to deliberate on key issues concerning highway development, project implementation and infrastructure delivery. Minister of State for Road Transport and Highways Shri Harsh Malhotra also addressed the inaugural session.
Addressing the inaugural session, Shri Gadkari said the Chintan Shivir provides an important platform for the Centre and States to think together, share field-level experiences and work together towards practical solutions for emerging challenges in highway development. He emphasised that successful practices adopted by different States should be shared, evaluated and replicated wherever appropriate to improve project implementation and infrastructure outcomes across the country.
The Minister stressed that highway development must remain focused on quality, safety, speed and world-class standards. He called for greater emphasis on advance planning and preparedness at the Detailed Project Report (DPR) stage, including proper surveys, alignment planning, land acquisition, utility shifting and timely statutory clearances. Better preparedness at the initial stage, he said, can help minimise delays, avoid cost escalation and improve the efficiency of highway projects.
Shri Gadkari highlighted that road safety must be integrated into highway planning and project design from the beginning. Identification of accident-prone locations and incorporation of appropriate safety interventions during the planning and construction stages can contribute towards safer highways and reduction in road accidents.
Underscoring the importance of highway infrastructure for national economic growth, the Minister said modern highways should provide seamless connectivity between cities, towns, ports, markets and industrial centres. Improved connectivity supports trade, investment, employment and overall economic activity. He called for coordinated efforts by the Centre, States and implementing agencies to ensure timely delivery of infrastructure in line with the country’s growing development and mobility requirements.
The two-day Chintan Shivir will feature key thematic sessions covering PM GatiShakti and integrated infrastructure planning; Land Acquisition and Bhoomi Rashi; Model Concession Agreements and Ratings; Designing Safe Highways and Green Highways; Road Safety and Toll Reform; and Quality Assurance and Project Monitoring. The sessions are aimed at addressing implementation challenges, sharing best practices and identifying practical and replicable solutions for more efficient highway development.
The Minister also called for wider adoption of new technologies, innovative construction practices and cost-effective materials to improve quality and reduce construction and maintenance costs. He encouraged States and implementing agencies to share innovations and field-level solutions and stressed the importance of research, technology and continuous improvement in highway construction and maintenance.
Sustainability and environmental responsibility form an important component of the Chintan Shivir’s agenda. Shri Gadkari emphasised the need to promote environment-friendly construction practices and greater use of innovative and recycled materials, while ensuring appropriate measures for environmental and wildlife protection. In this context, a document on Environment & Wildlife Mitigation Measures was launched during the inaugural session.
A BRICS Compendium on Perspectives in Sustainable Transport was also launched during the session, bringing together perspectives on sustainable approaches in the transport sector and adding an international dimension to the deliberations on future-ready infrastructure.
Shri Gadkari also highlighted technology-driven reforms aimed at improving the efficiency and convenience of highway travel, including FASTag Annual Pass and Multi-Lane Free Flow (MLFF). These initiatives reflect the Ministry’s continued focus on modernising tolling systems, improving traffic movement and enhancing the overall highway user experience.
The inaugural session set the broader direction for the deliberations ahead, with the Chintan Shivir providing a platform for Centre-State dialogue, exchange of experiences and best practices, and identification of innovative and replicable solutions. The discussions over the two days will seek to strengthen project planning and monitoring, improve highway quality and safety, promote sustainable infrastructure and accelerate the delivery of future-ready highway infrastructure.
Shri Gadkari called upon all stakeholders to work collectively towards safer, high-quality and future-ready highway infrastructure, contributing to faster economic growth and stronger connectivity in line with the vision of Viksit Bharat.

title: TDB-DST signs agreement with BigEndian Semiconductors for ₹130 crore RDI support to develop indigenous AI Vision SoC
subtitle: Project VeerAI to advance secure, application-specific semiconductor technology from TRL-5 to TRL-9
date:

                05 OCT 2026 12:23PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Strengthening India’s efforts to build indigenous semiconductor capabilities for critical and emerging applications, the Technology Development Board (TDB), Department of Science & Technology (DST), Government of India, has signed an agreement with M/s BigEndian Semiconductors, Bengaluru, Karnataka for financial support of ₹130 crore under the Research Development and Innovation (RDI) Fund.
The project, Project VeerAI, has a total project cost of ₹260 crore and aims to take the technology from Technology Readiness Level (TRL)-5 to TRL-9. The financial support will be provided through Optional Convertible Debt (OCD). Project VeerAI seeks to develop a camera-focused AI Vision System-on-Chip (SoC) on a sovereign technology platform, addressing the growing requirement for secure, intelligent and application-specific semiconductor solutions.
The project is positioned around the development of a secure AI chip for surveillance applications, particularly CCTV systems, with the objective of reducing dependence on externally developed semiconductor and technology supply chains. The proposed platform is designed to combine AI processing and smart features with security, privacy and connectivity capabilities. The technology is being developed initially for CCTV and surveillance applications in India and the Global South, with a roadmap for deployment across multiple sectors. Beyond surveillance, the platform is envisaged for applications in defence, automotive, industrial and medical domains, creating a wider market for indigenous AI-enabled semiconductor solutions.
The project also seeks to leverage India’s growing VLSI design and semiconductor talent, translating domestic design capabilities into a scalable product platform. By focusing on application-specific SoCs rather than general-purpose chips, the programme aims to address specific industry requirements while enabling faster technology deployment and commercialisation. The development of indigenous AI and semiconductor technologies has growing significance as connected devices and intelligent systems become increasingly embedded across critical infrastructure. Secure and application-specific chips can play an important role in addressing requirements related to data security, privacy, device-level intelligence and technology sovereignty.
Through the RDI support, BigEndian Semiconductors will undertake further technology development, validation, integration, testing and scale-up activities required to progress Project VeerAI from TRL-5 to TRL-9.
Sh. Rajesh Kumar Pathak, Secretary, TDB, said,
“Semiconductors are foundational to almost every emerging technology, and building indigenous capabilities in application-specific AI chips is an important part of strengthening India’s technology ecosystem. The RDI Fund enables sustained support for technologies that require significant investment to move from advanced development to commercial deployment. The support to BigEndian Semiconductors reflects TDB’s focus on enabling Indian companies to develop strategic semiconductor capabilities and translate domestic design expertise into deployable products.”
Promoters of BigEndian Semiconductors said,
“The RDI support from TDB will enable us to accelerate the development and validation of Project VeerAI and take our AI Vision SoC towards commercial readiness. Our focus is on building a secure, application-specific semiconductor platform that can address the requirements of surveillance and other critical sectors while leveraging India’s indigenous semiconductor design capabilities. This partnership will help us progress the technology towards TRL-9 and contribute to the development of a stronger domestic semiconductor ecosystem.”

title: Dibrugarh Sends First International Cargo from Bogibeel to Bangladesh Since Independence
subtitle:
Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal flags off 540 tonnes of APCL Methanol from Bogibeel to Dhaka, with Assam CM Dr Himanta Biswa Sarma joins virtually

Voyage on the Brahmaputra (NW-2) tests river as Freight Corridor Linking India's Northeast to Overseas Markets

The steamer whistle that fell silent in 1956 is heard again today: Sarbananda Sonowal
ministry: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                05 OCT 2026 4:02PM by PIB Delhi
content:
A barge carrying 540 metric tons of methanol left Bogibeel Terminal in Dibrugarh for Dhaka, Bangladesh, here today.
Sarbananda Sonowal, Union Minister of Ports, Shipping and Waterways (MoPSW)
, flagged off the vessel DLB Patkai, pushed by the tug Kushal Konwar from Bogibeel.
Assam Chief Minister Dr Himanta Biswa Sarma
joined the ceremony virtually. It is the first cargo shipped from the upper Assam to a foreign port since India's independence in 1947, nearly 70 years after the town's river ghat closed.
The methanol, produced by state-owned Assam Petro-Chemicals Ltd. (APCL) at Namrup, is bound for Pangaon Port in Dhaka, Bangladesh. The vessel will travel about 768 kilometres down National Waterway-2 on the Brahmaputra River in India to the Indo-Bangladesh border, then continue along the Indo-Bangladesh Protocol Route (IBPR). The vessel will cover a total distance of 1,300 kms from Bogibeel, Dibrugarh to Narayanganj, Dhaka.
The voyage is being observed as a test of whether the Brahmaputra can serve as a commercially viable freight corridor linking the Northeast to overseas markets. Regular methanol shipments to Bangladesh are planned. The shipment became possible after customs and immigration complexes were set up at Bogibeel and Dhubri recently.
"Our grandparents grew up hearing the steamer whistle at Dibrugarh Ghat. For 70 years, that whistle fell silent and the ships stopped coming," Sonowal said. "Today, a ship leaves Dibrugarh for the world once again. The river never failed us. What it lacked for decades was the will to revive it.”
Sarma called it a proud day for Assam. "Assam's own product, made in Namrup, is now traveling to an international market on Assam's own river, The Northeast is no longer a frontier. It is India's gateway to the East.” he said.
Sonowal said the shipment was a beginning. "This is the first voyage, not the last," he said. "To the youth of Assam I say: Dream with this river. The world is no longer far away. It is downstream. Under Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Dibrugarh, the Tea Capital of India, is reclaiming the glory it once had as a great river port. We are building it with world-class infrastructure while honouring its heritage. The steamer whistle that fell silent in 1956 is heard again,"
Sonowal
exclaimed.
Dibrugarh was once among the busiest river ports in eastern India. Government steamers reached the town from Calcutta, now Kolkata, by 1856. In 1882, the Dibru-Sadiya Railway began operating from the Dibrugarh steamer ghat. By 1913, steamers sailed up the Brahmaputra to the town daily, carrying tea, timber and passengers.
The 1947 partition cut that route, forcing Assam's goods to pass through East Pakistan to reach Calcutta. A 1950 earthquake disturbed the riverbed at Dibrugarh. Regular bookings from Dibrugarh Ghat stopped in 1954, and the ghat closed on October 15, 1956, as tea shipments shifted to rail. The 1965 war between India and Pakistan suspended cross-border river trade. India and Bangladesh signed a river trade protocol in 1972. In 1988, the 891-kilometer stretch of river Brahmaputra from Sadiya to Dhubri was declared National Waterway-2. Regular cargo service on the waterway did not begin until December 2017, when cement moved from Pandu to Dhubri.
"For decades, that glory was allowed to fade. Under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, we set out to give Dibrugarh back its rightful place. The Bogibeel terminal, the customs and immigration complex and fixed-schedule cargo services under ‘Jalvahak’ are giving this historic town modern amenities and world-class infrastructure. We are building for the future while reinstating the heritage that made Dibrugarh great. Today, as cargo leaves Dibrugarh for a foreign port once again, the town's proud past and its promising future meet on the same river,” Sonowal added.
Activity on the route has grown since then. Tata Steel barges reached Pandu through Bangladesh in February 2022, and the river cruise ship MV Ganga Vilas sailed from Varanasi to Dibrugarh through Bangladesh in 2023. The Bogibeel passenger and cargo terminal, whose foundation stone was laid in July 2023, opened in February 2024. The ‘Jalvahak' cargo incentive program launched in December 2024.
According to the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways (MoPSW), cargo on India's national waterways rose from 18 million metric tons in fiscal 2013-14 to 218 million metric tons in 2025-26. More than 68 billion rupees (about $770 million) is being invested in waterways across the Northeast, including development of National Waterway-2, a ship repair facility at Pandu and last-mile connectivity to Pandu Port.
"Every ton we move on the river means less fuel burnt and fewer trucks on the highway," Sonowal said. He added that India is working with Bangladesh, Nepal, Bhutan and Myanmar on regional waterway links.
The voyage involved the Inland Waterways Authority of India, Assam Petro-Chemicals, Cochin Bunkers Pvt. Ltd. and partners in Bangladesh.
Assam state ministers
Charan Boro, Bimal Borah
and
Sushanta Borgohain
attended, along with
Terash Gowalla
, a member of the Rajya Sabha, the upper house of India's Parliament. Also present were state legislators from the region, including
Prasanta Phukan
,
MLA, Dibrugarh LAC
and
Chakradhar Gogoi, MLA, Khowang LAC.
IWAI’s Chief Engineer, AK Bansal
and
Assam Petro-Chemicals APCL’s Chairman, Bikul Ch. Deka
was
also present along with officials of APCL, IWAI and Govt of Assam attended the historic event.

title: National Household Travel Survey July, 2025 – June, 2026
subtitle:

 ‘Two-Wheelers Lead Workforce Mobility’
date:

                05 OCT 2026 4:00PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Snapshots
NSO conducted the first-ever all-India survey on household travel, covering 14,274 villages and 10,377 urban blocks. The survey collected information from 4,92,023 households, covering 20,34,371 persons.
Two-wheelers are the predominant mode of transport for commuting to fixed workplaces, accounting for 42.6% of workers.
Overnight trips undertaken by households are primarily for social and religious purposes, with buses being the predominant mode of transport.
Around 87.6% of students reach their educational institutions within 30 minutes, while 83.4% of workers commute to their fixed workplaces in less than 30 minutes.
The average monthly expenditure on commuting to a fixed workplace is ₹785 per worker. Urban workers incur a substantially higher average monthly cost of ₹1,044, compared with ₹612 for rural workers.
The National Statistics Office (NSO) under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) has released the key indicators and findings from the
first ever National Household Travel Survey (NHTS)
, conducted during July, 2025 – June, 2026 through a Factsheet. For the purpose of the survey, a trip is defined as travel covering a distance of more than 1 km.
Primary objectives of the survey
The primary objective of the survey is to generate robust, data-driven insights into domestic travel patterns and dynamics to support regional transport planning, infrastructure development and evidence-based policy formulation. The survey captures key aspects of domestic travel, including:
Purpose of travel: Employment, education, social engagements, cultural and leisure activities, tourism, domestic work, caregiving and other purposes.
Mode of transport: Modes of transportation used by different demographic groups for undertaking trips.
Travel duration and distance: Average time taken and distances travelled during trips.
In addition to meeting the specific data requirements of the Ministry of Railways, the survey is expected to provide valuable insights into
how, when and why people travel
. The information collected on travel patterns and public transport usage will help identify gaps in existing transport systems, assess accessibility, optimise transport routes and improve service frequency and scheduling. The findings will also provide an important evidence base for regional transportation planning, infrastructure investment and the formulation of informed transport policies.
Major Findings
The major findings of NHTS on four central aspects of commuting, namely, (i) mobility, (ii) duration & peak hours, (iii) expenditure involved, and (iv) overnight and non-work travel are summarised below:
Student Mobility
66.4% of Students Commute More Than 1 km Daily:
Nearly two-third of students aged 6 years and above undertake within-travel-day trips of at least 1 km to attend their basic course educational institution (65.6% in rural areas; 68.1% in urban areas). Trips less than one kilometre were not recorded. North-eastern States, including Assam and neighbouring States, show considerable less travel time (15 to 19 minutes).
77.0% Peak Mobility in Youth (15-29 Years):
Students aged 15 - 29 years record the highest regular trip participation at 79.1% in rural India and 73.3% in urban India for daily commute to attend educational Institutes.
Top 3 Modes to Power School Trips:
Walking (37.0%), Buses (29.5%), and Bicycles (15.8%) account for the vast majority of student commutes nationwide.
Auto-Rickshaws & Two-Wheelers in Student Transit:
Auto-rickshaws serve 10.5% of commuting students overall (rising to 14.4% in urban areas), while two-wheelers account for 6.7% (11.5% in urban areas).
Workforce Mobility
57.6% of Workers Travel More Than 1 km to Work:
Over half of all workers aged 15 years and above perform within-travel-day trips to fixed or non-fixed workplaces (54.5% rural vs. 64.1% urban).
States such as Rajasthan, Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh show average travel times of around 20–23 minutes, with higher travel times in parts of southern India.
Gender Gap in Workforce Travel:
61.9% of male workers undertake daily work trips (>1 km) compared to 41.9% of female workers nationwide.
42.6% of Workers Ride Two-Wheelers:
Two-wheelers are the single largest primary mode of transport for workers across India (37.1% rural; 52.3% urban).
Urban Mass Transit Hotspots:
While monorail, metro, suburban rail, and trams account for 5.0% of urban worker commutes nationally, usage surges in Maharashtra (20.7%), West Bengal (16.5%), and Delhi (14.4%).
Commute Duration & Peak Hours
23 Minutes to School | 25 Minutes to Work:
Average travel time from origin is 23 minutes for students (23 min rural; 22 min urban) and 25 minutes for workers travelling to a fixed workplace (23 min rural; 27 min urban).
87.6% of Students Reach Within 30 Minutes:
Nearly 9 in 10 students complete their journey to educational institutions in up to 30 minutes (86.6% rural; 89.6% urban).
83.4% of Workers Commute in Under 30 Minutes:
Over four-fifth of workers reach their fixed workplace within half an hour (86.1% rural; 79.3% urban), while 13.7% take 30 - 60 minutes.
82.0% of Students Depart Between 7:00 AM & 10:00 AM:
Peak school departure occurs between 8:00 - 9:00 AM (35.7%), followed by 7:00 - 8:00 AM (26.6%) and 9:00 - 10:00 AM (19.7%).
94.9% of Workers Leave Before 10:00 AM:
Morning rush hour for fixed workplaces peaks between 8:00 - 10:00 AM (56.5%) and 6:00 - 8:00 AM (33.7%), with 4.7% leaving before 6:00 AM.
Monthly Commute Expenditure
Average Student Commute Cost - ₹443/Month:
Urban students spend an average of ₹617 per month on trips to and from educational institutions, compared to ₹361 per month in rural India.
Average Worker Commute Cost - ₹785/Month:
Workers commuting to a fixed workplace spend ₹1044 per month in urban areas and ₹612 per month in rural areas.
Gender Disparity in Worker Travel Spend:
Male workers spend an average of ₹835 per month on fixed-workplace commutes compared to ₹533 per month for female workers.
Overnight & Non-Work Travel
73.5% of Overnight Trips Rely on Bus & Rail:
Buses (55.8%) and inter-city railways (17.7%) are the primary modes for household overnight travel, followed by cars (15.1%) and two-wheelers (8.8%).
22.7% of Urban Households Choose Rail for Overnight Trips:
Railway usage for overnight journeys is about 14.0% among rural households and around 22.7% among urban households.
70.2% of Overnight Travel is Social & Religious:
Socializing, communication, and religious activities drive the overwhelming majority of overnight household trips (69.7% rural; 70.9% urban).
Tourism & Health in Overnight Travel
: Culture, leisure, sports, and tourism account for 7.4% of overnight household trips (9.3% in urban areas), while self-care and maintenance account for 6.5% (7.6% in rural areas).
Other Daily Trips - Two-Wheelers, Walking & Autos Lead:
For within-day trips other than education and employment, citizens primarily use two-wheelers (32.2%), walking (24.9%), auto-rickshaws (18.9%), bicycles (12.6%), and buses (8.5%).
Estimates of indicators of the related parameters at all-India level for both rural and urban sectors are given in the enclosed Appendix.
Appendix
Key features and conceptual framework of the survey
The survey collected data on regular travels of
one kilometre or more
performed by Indian people. It was aimed at collecting information on the modes of transport they use, trip purposes, travel frequency, average cost incurred for regular trips and other related parameters. Covering both rural and urban areas across all States and Union Territories of India, this nationwide survey will be a comprehensive benchmark for understanding characteristics of household travel behaviour in the country.
The following new concepts have been introduced in this first ever all India survey.
‘
Travel’
in NHTS covers only those trips which entails traversing a distance of one km or more. Any trip of less than one km was not considered a ‘
travel’
in NHTS.
‘Primary mode of travel’
means any mode of transport that was used to traverse the longest distance during a trip. If a trip was performed by using a single mode of transport, that will decisively be the primary mode
Travel-day:
For all purpose of the household travel survey, a travel day will refer to the duration starting from 3:00 AM of one calendar day to 2:59 AM of the next calendar day.
Within travel-day trips:
Trips that ended anytime during a travel-day and do not keep the household member(s) away from their residence for longer than 24 hours was considered as within travel-day trip. Such trips may span over at most two consecutive travel-days.
Overnight trip:
A trip that kept a member away from their residence for more than 24 hours will be considered as overnight trip. This will include the travel time as well as duration of stay, if any, during the trip. However, such trips of lengths less than 50 km were not considered as overnight trip even if it kept the household member(s) away from their residence for more than 24 hours:

date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                05 OCT 2026 8:13PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Ministry of Textiles observed
Gandhi Jayanti
on 2 October 2026 with a series of
Swachhta and cleanliness activities under Special Campaign 6.0
, reaffirming its commitment to promoting cleanliness, hygiene and a culture of responsible workplace practices.
The programme was led by
Secretary (Textiles) at the National Institute of Fashion Technology (NIFT), Delhi
, and was attended by senior officers of the Ministry of Textiles, faculty members and staff of NIFT Delhi. On the occasion, the
Swachhta Pledge
was administered, with participants reaffirming their commitment to maintaining cleanliness and contributing towards a cleaner and healthier environment.
A cleanliness drive was also undertaken at the NIFT Delhi campus, with active participation of officers, faculty and staff. The activities focused on improving cleanliness and upkeep of the premises, promoting proper waste management and sensitising participants towards maintaining clean and hygienic surroundings.
The observance of Gandhi Jayanti under
Special Campaign 6
underscores the Ministry of Textiles’ continued efforts to institutionalise
Swachhta
in its offices and field establishments and to encourage collective participation in creating clean, well-maintained and sustainable workplaces. The Ministry continues to accord priority to cleanliness, disposal of obsolete and unusable items, better workplace management and sustained improvement in cleanliness standards as part of the Special Campaign.
Textile Waste Collection Drive starting this Gandhi Jayanti
As part of the initiative, starting this Gandhi Jayanti, 2nd October 2026, a dedicated textile waste collection bins have been installed at various locations. The initiative seeks to further strengthen the spirit of Jan Bhagidari and collective action towards a clean and sustainable India, with emphasis on cleanliness, responsible waste management, and the adoption of sustainable practices.
The initiative aims to promote responsible collection, segregation, recycling and upcycling of post-consumer textile waste and to encourage sustainable waste-management practices in Central Government office complexes and residential colonies in New Delhi. All officers and officials have been requested to actively participate in the drive by bringing and depositing their post-consumer textile waste in the designated collection bins during the campaign period
As part of the Implementation Phase of Special Campaign 6, Officers and employees of the attached and subordinate offices of Ministry of Textiles actively participated in the Swachhta Pledge, reaffirming their commitment towards cleanliness, hygiene and maintaining a clean and sustainable working environment.
As part of the campaign, a comprehensive cleanliness and de-cluttering drive was undertaken at the National Jute Board premises at Patsan Bhawan, Kolkata, and the Regional Office, New Delhi, from 2nd to 4th October 2026

The Ministry of Textiles continues to make concerted efforts towards achieving the objectives of Special Campaign 6, with a particular focus on Swachhta, cleanliness, space management, disposal of pending references and e-waste management.
